We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps: 1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (forward). So retrosynthesis: break amide to carboxylic acid and amine.

2) Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (alkene). So retrosynthesis: break the C=C double bond and carboxylic acid to aldehyde and malonic acid? Actually forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (with decarboxylation). So retro: from α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid.

Our target contains a α,β-unsaturated amide: /C=C/C(=O)N... The unsaturated part is from Doebner? Actually Doebner gives unsaturated acid, then amide formation gives unsaturated amide. So step 2: break the C=C and the carboxylic acid (which is now amide after step1). In retrosynthesis, we can disconnect the C=C to give an aldehyde (aryl aldehyde) and malonic acid.

3) Sulfonamide formation: sulfonyl chloride + amine -> sulfonamide. So retro: break sulfonamide to sulfonyl chloride and amine.

Thus overall: target -> break amide to give unsaturated acid + aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then break unsaturated acid via Doebner to give aldehyde (aryl aldehyde) and malonic acid. Then break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (ArSO2Cl) and aniline (the first aromatic amine). The sulfonyl chloride derived from p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually target has sulfonamide attached to p-tolyl (Cc1ccc...). So sulfonyl chloride is p-tolylsulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-CH3). The amine is the other aromatic ring (c2ccc...).

Thus propose route:

Step 1 (retro): amide bond cleavage: product: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid fragment: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Wait need to be precise. The amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). So cleavage gives α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (the part with sulfonamide attached) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The unsaturated acid is: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Actually the acid part is the aryl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring with a side chain: /C=C/COOH? The target has /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. So after breaking amide, we have /C=C/COOH attached to the sulfonamide phenyl. So fragment A: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1 (the aryl sulfonamide with unsaturated acid). Fragment B: aniline (c3ccccc3N). Good.

Step 2 (retro): break the α,β-unsaturated acid via Doebner: gives aldehyde (aryl aldehyde) and malonic acid. The aldehyde is the aryl sulfonamide phenyl with aldehyde at position where the side chain attaches: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2)cc1. The malonic acid is HOOC-CH2-COOH.

Step 3 (retro): break sulfonamide: gives p-tolylsulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-CH3) and the aryl amine (the aldehyde phenyl with NH2). Actually the sulfonamide is attached to the first phenyl (p-tolyl) and the second phenyl (the aldehyde phenyl). In our fragment after step2, the sulfonamide is still present linking the two phenyls. To break it, we need sulfonyl chloride (p-tolylsulfonyl chloride) and the aryl amine (the aldehyde phenyl with NH2). So fragment after step3: p-tolylsulfonyl chloride and 4-aminobenzaldehyde (or appropriate substitution). The aldehyde phenyl also has NH2 (since sulfonamide broken, the amine becomes free). So we get 4-aminobenzaldehyde (or 4-aminophenyl aldehyde) with the aldehyde at para to the amine? In target, the sulfonamide attaches at para position relative to methyl on p-tolyl, and at para position relative to aldehyde on the other phenyl. So the amine after cleavage is 4-aminobenzaldehyde.

Thus final precursors: p-tolylsulfonyl chloride, 4-aminobenzaldehyde, malonic acid.

Now we need to construct JSON route with three reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for each step. We can search for templates for amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). Search for functional_groups_broken: carboxylic acid, formed: amide. Use correct functional group name: "aliphatic carboxylic acid" or "aromatic carboxylic acid". Our acid is aromatic unsaturated acid (aryl). So use "aromatic carboxylic acid". Let's search.
